calls.reason: OpenAI's own InstructGPT paper reports hallucination rates of 41% for GPT-3 and 21% for InstructGPT, and says the model still makes simple mistakes. PaLM solved only 58% of GSM8K. Both point to continuing unreliability in early 2022.
TRIP tested only BERT-family models on physical reasoning, while PaLM showed strong commonsense results. No evidence covers both domains or settles whether the weakness is inherent.
The only full-set comparison is coauthored by Marcus and Davis. Alexander's independent test covered six earlier failures, so it cannot show the overall size of the change or any backsliding.

The InstructGPT paper shows general mistakes and PaLM shows strong benchmark progress. Neither checks the six named problem categories one by one, so the claim that all core claims still hold cannot be judged.
TruthfulQA and the InstructGPT paper show the models were easy to trip up, but nothing in the packet measures genuine comprehension or shows that missing comprehension is the cause.
The GPT-4 launch notes describe a staged rollout. There is no record that Marcus and Davis got unrestricted access, that GPT-4 met the same-architecture condition, or of their first day of testing.
